title: Abdallah bin Ma'amar

full_text:
Abdallah bin Ma'amar was the governor of Basra in the golden days of the Abbasid Caliphate, revered by his people as a ruler who combined firm justice with the tenderest compassion for the poor and the troubled.

One evening, as Abdallah was returning from inspecting the public granaries, he heard the sounds of bitter lamentation coming from an ancient cemetery. Dismounting from his mule, he entered the quiet tombs and found a handsome young Bedouin weeping beside a freshly dug grave.

Abdallah approached gently, placed a hand upon his shoulder, and asked: 'What great sorrow has brought you to weep among the dead, my son?'

The young man wiped his tears and answered: 'O noble traveler, I am Utbah, son of a desert shaykh. For five years, my cousin Rayya and I have loved each other with pure affection. But her father, demanding an exorbitant dowry of fifty pedigree camels and a thousand gold dinars which my impoverished father could not provide, has betrothed her against her will to an affluent stranger from Damascus. Tomorrow she departs, and my soul is already dead.'

Abdallah’s heart was touched by the youth’s sincere devotion. He lifted Utbah to his feet and said: 'Do not despair, for hope is never dead while justice lives.'

The governor immediately dispatched messengers to the bride’s father and the Syrian suitor, inviting them to his palace.

Before the council, Abdallah spoke with eloquent passion on the sanctity of true love and the cruelty of treating children as merchandise. He then opened his own treasury, paid the full dowry of fifty fine camels and a thousand gold dinars on Utbah’s behalf, and compensated the Syrian suitor with rare silks and jewels from his personal stores.

The bride’s father, moved to tears and ashamed of his greed, joyfully bestowed his daughter upon Utbah. The happy union was celebrated across Basra with feasts that lasted three days, and Abdallah bin Ma'amar was blessed by all the people as the protector of faithful hearts.
moral: Generous intervention that reconciles estranged lovers and heals family rifts is the highest duty of a noble leader.
